subject: science
title: US Middle School Science - Plate Tectonics and Natural Hazards
subtitle: Earth layers, plate boundaries, earthquakes, volcanoes, tsunamis, and hazard risk reduction.
description: A source-faithful revision pack covering how tectonic plates move, how boundary types shape Earth, and how earthquakes, volcanoes, and tsunamis create risks. Students practise key vocabulary, compare evidence, order processes, interpret hazard patterns, and explain mitigation using scientific reasoning.

data.sentence: The rigid outer layer made of the crust and uppermost mantle is the ____.
data.hint: It is broken into tectonic plates.

data.sentence: The softer upper mantle layer beneath the lithosphere is the ____.
data.hint: Plates move above this layer.

data.sentence: At a ____ boundary, plates move apart and new crust can form.
data.hint: Think of mid-ocean ridges.

data.sentence: At a ____ boundary, plates slide past each other sideways.
data.hint: The San Andreas Fault is an example.

data.sentence: At a ____ boundary, plates move toward each other.
data.hint: This can involve collision or subduction.

data.sentence: The process where one plate sinks beneath another is called ____.
data.hint: It often involves dense oceanic crust.

data.sentence: An underwater mountain range where new oceanic crust forms is a ____.
data.hint: New crust spreads outward from it.

data.sentence: A deep underwater valley at many subduction zones is a ____.
data.hint: It forms where one plate bends downward.

data.sentence: The point underground where an earthquake begins is the ____.
data.hint: The epicenter is above it.

data.sentence: The point on Earth's surface directly above the earthquake focus is the ____.
data.hint: It is a surface location.

data.sentence: Earthquake ____ measures the energy released by an earthquake.
data.hint: It is not the same as local damage.

data.sentence: Melted rock below the surface is ____, but melted rock at the surface is lava.
data.hint: Below ground is the clue.

data.sentence: Magma becomes ____ when it reaches Earth's surface.
data.hint: This happens during an eruption.

data.sentence: A ____ is a series of large ocean waves often caused by sudden seafloor movement.
data.hint: It is not an ordinary wind wave.

data.sentence: The ____ is a Pacific Ocean zone with many earthquakes and volcanoes.
data.hint: It surrounds much of the Pacific Ocean.

data.sentence: The San Andreas Fault is mainly a ____ boundary.
data.hint: The plates slide past each other.

data.sentence: The Himalaya Mountains formed from a ____ collision.
data.hint: Two continents pushed together.

data.sentence: The Hawaiian Islands are explained by a ____ under a moving plate.
data.hint: They are not mainly at a plate boundary.

data.sentence: Earthquake-resistant buildings are designed to flex and absorb ____ energy.
data.hint: This reduces collapse risk.

data.sentence: A hazard becomes a disaster when it causes serious ____ to people, property, or ecosystems.
data.hint: Preparedness can reduce it.

data.sentence: GPS evidence shows that plates are still moving by measuring small changes in ____ over time.
data.hint: GPS tracks location precisely.

data.sentence: Similar fossils on continents now separated by oceans suggest those continents were once ____.
data.hint: This supports plate tectonics.

data.title: How an Earthquake Happens
data.instruction: Put the earthquake process in the correct order.
items: Tectonic forces push or pull rocks near a fault.
Friction causes rocks to lock while stress builds.
Stress becomes greater than the strength of the rocks.
Rocks suddenly slip along the fault.
Stored energy travels outward as seismic waves.
The ground shakes and aftershocks may follow.

data.title: How a Tsunami Can Form
data.instruction: Put the tsunami formation steps in the correct order.
items: A strong shallow underwater earthquake moves the seafloor vertically.
Ocean water above the moving seafloor is displaced.
Waves spread outward across the ocean.
The waves slow down as they enter shallow water near shore.
Water piles up and can flood coastal areas with strong currents.

data.title: Volcano Formation at a Subduction Zone
data.instruction: Put the subduction volcano steps in the correct order.
items: A dense oceanic plate moves toward another plate.
The oceanic plate subducts into the mantle.
Water and materials from the sinking plate help mantle rock melt.
Magma forms and rises through the crust.
Lava, ash, and gases can erupt at the surface.

data.title: From Observation to Plate Tectonics
data.instruction: Order the evidence-based reasoning from observation to explanation.
items: Scientists observe matching fossils, rocks, seafloor stripes, and earthquake patterns.
They compare the observations across continents and ocean floors.
They notice that many patterns line up with plate boundaries.
They use seafloor spreading and GPS data to show plates move.
They explain Earth features using the theory of plate tectonics.
